requirements.title: Default provider campaign
requirements.behaviour: Play and Continue open a management campaign. Training, Lab and the retained SP game are separate experiences.
acceptance: A fresh normal run requires only a provider name, home market and difficulty, all with defaults.
The first view contains an objective, finite capital, a customer opportunity and a costed action. No JSON or pack-start buttons are required.
Existing training and SP saves remain separately accessible.

requirements.title: Campaign authority boundary
requirements.behaviour: Separate player actions, scenario authorship and evaluation at the shared dispatcher, including nested customer commands.
acceptance: Campaign attempts to set supplier cost, arbitrary capacity, customer requirements, fault events, task success or quality grades fail atomically through UI, worker and MCP paths.
Retail quotation is permitted only through authored customer acceptance rules.
No public system:true or arbitrary-command escape hatch is added; Lab editing remains available on a custom copy.

requirements.title: Purchased starting estate
requirements.behaviour: Start with one home market, a finite team and purchasable capability. Canonical resource IDs may exist as dormant internal blueprints.
acceptance: Uncommissioned blueprints supply no usable entitlement, service, capacity or revenue.
Buying a supported plan creates its necessary dependencies through validated commands without asking the player to start internal packs.
Ownership and entitlement gate later capacity changes.

requirements.title: One explicit clock
requirements.behaviour: Retain integer simulation minutes and 60-minute billing periods. Initial pacing is 1 simulation minute per 2 real seconds at 1x.
acceptance: Pause and 0.5x/1x/2x/4x/8x are available. Prices use /period, never an unexplained /month.
Equal simulation-time commands at different speeds yield identical demand, outcomes, balances and rewards.
Decision modals, hidden tabs, lost editing ownership and terminal outcomes pause; no undisclosed offline catch-up occurs.

requirements.title: Atomic quotes and purchases
requirements.behaviour: A pure quote explains upfront cost, recurring commitments, lead time, labour, capacity and consequences. Commit recalculates against the current revision.
acceptance: Stale or unaffordable quotes cannot double-spend or create partial inventory.
Repeating the same request ID does not charge, reserve or reward twice.
The client supplies offer and recipe identifiers, not authoritative wholesale cost or success.

requirements.title: One provider treasury
requirements.behaviour: All customers share one parent cash balance, credit agreement and provider team. Customer views are attributed subledgers.
acceptance: Creating a second customer does not create opening cash.
Internal transfers do not become external revenue, and settlement receipts post once.
Cash available excludes reservations; cash, commitments, liabilities and operating profit remain distinguishable.

requirements.title: Funding and insolvency
requirements.behaviour: Enforce upfront affordability and authored credit limits, and model unpaid posted obligations as visible arrears/default states.
acceptance: The unfunded 20-engineer, 1,440-minute project repro cannot start without an explicit funded or credit-backed commitment.
An unavoidable bill can enter grace/default without crashing the engine or enabling unlimited discretionary spending.
Forecast recurring exposure before commitment; do not escrow every future cost unless the scenario requires it.

requirements.title: Separate success states
requirements.behaviour: Tutorial, service readiness, contract delivery, operating profit, progression and mission victory use distinct state and labels.
acceptance: Passing the four-command foundation SMB repair cannot complete a provider campaign.
A probe or manually generated test cannot mint earned customer revenue or commercial progression.
Every mission authors arrivals, deadlines, activation, service/credit/renewal rules, grace/default and a sustained victory predicate.

The proposed SMB reference requires two consecutive full periods with at least 22 of 24 due cases completed on time and positive provider operating result, no overdue critical obligations, and a funded next contract. A quiet or partial period cannot satisfy it.

requirements.title: Versioned experience and saves
requirements.behaviour: Add a versioned experience discriminator without repurposing guided/assessed/sandbox or the existing SOC_CAMPAIGN training scheduler.
acceptance: Legacy guided/assessed imports remain Training and legacy sandbox imports remain Lab.
A campaign exported to Lab is custom; changing a label does not restore earned campaign status.
Validate with the known old schema before migration, preserve the original, and reject unknown versions clearly.

requirements.title: Autonomous customer work
requirements.behaviour: Seeded campaign demand produces customer jobs through the authoritative simulation and drives visible service flows.
acceptance: Calls, messages and CC arrivals appear without Generate test interaction.
Sampled particles and traces do not create or bill additional work.
Offered, admitted, pending, completed, failed and abandoned totals conserve jobs across handoff and retry.

requirements.title: Period-history settlement
requirements.behaviour: Accumulate service, usage and obligation history throughout the period and settle each contract from that history.
acceptance: An evenly distributed test workload with 57 minutes of outage cannot become a perfect period after a last-minute repair.
A final-minute outage cannot erase completed service from the prior 59 minutes.
Credits, usage, renewal evidence and visible bill explanations agree with the same recorded facts.

requirements.title: Duration-bearing ordinary calls
requirements.behaviour: Ordinary calls occupy the appropriate capacity over a connected phase; probes are separate.
acceptance: An endpoint call with a declared duration produces the expected occupancy and metered usage.

Immediate connectivity probes do not count as completed commercial conversations. Existing synchronous consumers such as siteHooks.journey migrate to explicit probes or asynchronous delivery evidence.
Waiting, talk time, connected carrier-leg occupancy and customer-billed units have explicit definitions.

requirements.title: Live media consequences
requirements.behaviour: Active ordinary calls and meetings continuously evaluate their effective media path and supported fallback.
acceptance: Loss of both media directions during a call cannot silently yield a successful conversation.
One-way media produces its declared degraded/failed outcome.
Loss of signalling alone does not automatically destroy surviving established media; local fallback must be provisioned.

requirements.title: Admission and reservations
requirements.behaviour: Use consistent admission, reservation and exactly-once release for constrained sessions, recording, meetings, people and processors.
acceptance: Capacity-one recording cannot capture four simultaneous recording-required sessions.
No available room/meeting capacity prevents an additional admission.
Cancellation, timeout, failure, normal completion and migration each release reservations once under a declared policy.

requirements.title: Scarce provider labour
requirements.behaviour: Deployment, migration, investigation, repair and bulk administration consume finite provider work capacity.
acceptance: Two simultaneous jobs cannot allocate the same engineer or reserved money twice.
Reduced support capacity increases eligible backlog/response time; reducing staff is not an identical-outcome cost saving.
Cost coherent operations, not each field write; inspection and planning stay free.

requirements.title: Two viable opening plans
requirements.behaviour: Author at least two sustainable opening solutions with different cost, lead time, margin, resilience or flexibility.
acceptance: A player can afford each reference plan individually but cannot buy every advantage without sacrificing another opportunity.
A changed supported seed/constraint changes a relevant investment or response.
The evaluator accepts outcomes and constraints, not only one exact recipe.

requirements.title: Upstream game frame
requirements.behaviour: Reuse upstream hierarchy and visual language: full-screen world, compact HUD, goals/deals/incidents navigation and contextual inspector.
acceptance: At 1366x768, cash, clock, objective, map and primary actions are reachable without scrolling through setup.
The default opening has no oversized hero or stacked module forms.
Match the bright map, white sticker panels, ink outlines, yellow actions and pink player selection with readable states.

requirements.title: Playable service map
requirements.behaviour: Project actual purchased suppliers, tenants, sites, platforms, integrations and workload paths into a selectable map.
acceptance: Purchasing, commissioning, losing and retiring a service visibly changes the correct nodes/paths.
Drag or click-connect opens a compatible costed plan; a keyboard/menu action does the same.
Region/geography, service dependencies and flows are selectable layers; graphics never grant service capability.

requirements.title: Contextual decision cards
requirements.behaviour: Expose a few relevant verbs for the selected scope, using supported choices and readable consequences.
acceptance: A purchase card names the cost now, /period commitment, work, lead time, limits and expected outcome.
An incident card names affected customers, cause confidence, response options and each cost/delay.
Blocked actions explain prerequisites and a way forward; no silent disabled button.

requirements.title: Stable UI during ticks
requirements.behaviour: Retain DOM identity or use keyed updates so simulation updates do not reset user work.
acceptance: An unfinished purchase draft retains values, focus, selection, scroll and expanded details during ticks.
Camera and selected customer persist across ordinary events.
Revalidate a changed quote at commit and explain any difference without silently accepting it.

requirements.title: Accessible equivalent controls
requirements.behaviour: Provide keyboard and screen-reader operation alongside the canvas, plus touch and reduced-motion support.
acceptance: The opening can be completed without drag, hover or colour-only information.
At 390x844, bottom navigation/context sheets preserve the same actions without horizontal page overflow.
Use visible focus, labelled status, restrained live announcements and at least 44px primary touch targets.

requirements.title: Readable consequences
requirements.behaviour: Show service results, customer impact, reservations, progress and earned money at the action location and in a short event feed.
acceptance: Provisioning, effective readiness and observed success are visibly distinct.
A player can open a bill or failure explanation without raw trace codes.
Optional sound and sampled animations reflect real events; both can be disabled.

requirements.title: Six-step coaching
requirements.behaviour: Guide actual play using state-based goals and highlights; show alternatives instead of prescribing every field.
acceptance: The six steps cover launch, external connection, partner capability, operation, expansion and a larger contract.

Coaching can be dismissed/resumed and recognises valid states reached out of order. An accepted order may satisfy an ordering milestone; it cannot satisfy commissioned service. Highlight Resume as soon as pending delivery is needed.
First costed choice within 2 minutes and first delivered work within 5 minutes are measured design targets, not claims of current performance.

requirements.title: Optional diagnosis
requirements.behaviour: Translate traces and dependencies into service explanations; keep raw records behind an advanced diagnostics view.
acceptance: The main inspector answers what is happening, who is affected, the likely cause and useful actions.
Experts can inspect detailed interaction paths, desired/effective state and evidence without editing world facts.
Diagnosis can consume time/effort when the scenario makes it a decision; looking at public information is free.

requirements.title: Consequential incidents
requirements.behaviour: Seed incidents from owned dependencies and scenario risk with meaningful recovery or mitigation choices.
acceptance: At least one mission incident has two sensible responses with different cost, time or customer loss.
Earlier redundancy, staffing or architecture changes impact or available responses.
A Repair action creates an eligible costed job; it cannot directly declare the service recovered.

requirements.title: Renewal, price and customer choice
requirements.behaviour: Customers consider authored service needs, price, delivered outcomes and switching friction.
acceptance: The player may quote retail prices but cannot force willingness to pay or contract acceptance.
Repeated poor service triggers bounded credits, lost demand, refusal/exit or scenario failure under visible terms.
An unavailable arbitrarily expensive offer cannot create an indefinitely repeatable profit strategy.

requirements.title: Commercial progression
requirements.behaviour: Success unlocks new contracts, capabilities, supplier terms, markets or useful automation.
acceptance: The first sustainable customer changes the next available decision.
Training badges/credits remain separate from earned commercial money and progress.
Next-goal requirements and blocked opportunities are visible with reasons.

requirements.title: Automation with tradeoffs
requirements.behaviour: Let mastered work become templates, scoped policy and scheduled operations that consume appropriate capacity and cost.
acceptance: A bulk joiner or migration template reduces repeated effort without bypassing entitlement or delegation.
Standing orders respect cash floors, budgets and capacity caps.
Automation shows a preview, commits once and can be suspended.

requirements.title: Portfolio continuity
requirements.behaviour: All active customers advance on one provider clock regardless of which customer is selected.
acceptance: Changing the inspector does not pause a tenant, reset a bill or move world revision.
An incident at one tenant competes with other work for shared staff and funds while preserving tenant authority.
Cancellation and decommission respect outstanding obligations and show the consequences before commitment.

requirements.title: Workload substitution
requirements.behaviour: Model WhatsApp/Messenger, workplace chat/Slack and video as eligible workload alternatives and competing propositions.
acceptance: A supported customer preference change alters a quote, channel investment, capacity plan or margin.
Substitution cannot remove PSTN, emergency, identity, information-boundary or other mandatory requirements.
Voice-to-digital handoff preserves one customer case; it cannot claim two independent resolutions.

requirements.title: Finance and operating report
requirements.behaviour: Present period revenue, usage, wholesale costs, payroll, credits, commitments and net operating result separately.
acceptance: A player can reconcile the displayed bill and cash movement to named economic events.
Borrowing/investment changes cash and debt, not operating profit.
Diagnostic/core counters are never labelled as commercial treasury.

requirements.title: SMB campaign
requirements.behaviour: A complete SMB mission makes capital, price, delivery speed and a small workforce matter.
acceptance: Includes a costed calling/contact service, demand, an incident, settlement, renewal/exit and a second opportunity.
Two plans or operating responses are viable and differ in margin, flexibility or risk.
A remembered tutorial recipe is not the only accepted solution.

requirements.title: Enterprise campaign
requirements.behaviour: A complete enterprise mission covers mixed estate migration and continuity with rooms/interoperability and contact-centre work.
acceptance: Staged coexistence and a more consolidated rollout create different staffing, time and compatibility consequences.
Actual number/identity/room dependencies affect work during cutover and recovery.
Settlement and renewal reflect the delivered migration and service outcomes.

requirements.title: Government campaign
requirements.behaviour: A complete government mission imposes authored processing, storage, retention, administration/support and delegated-access constraints.
acceptance: Eligibility follows actual paths and versioned evidence, not only a country field.
Two compliant architecture/operating plans differ in cost, lead time or workload.
A boundary or evidence change produces a visible service/procurement consequence and a valid repair.

requirements.title: Defence campaign
requirements.behaviour: A complete defence mission requires declared local operation, dependency survival and controlled reconnection.
acceptance: Pre-provisioned local identity, licensing, media, storage and processing determine supported survival during isolation.
Spares, staffing, autonomy duration and deferred synchronisation create real choices.
Reconnection applies scoped synchronisation and retained obligations; no real security accreditation is implied.

requirements.title: Microsoft family pathways
requirements.behaviour: Connect the existing six Microsoft-oriented family profiles to playable offers, dependencies and customer outcomes.
acceptance: Each of workplace calling, meetings/rooms, contact centre, communications APIs, government profiles and local deployment has at least one representative playable path tested through the campaign UI for this revision.
A family is not counted complete because its name appears in a menu.
Supplier-owned capabilities, third-party additions and scenario fiction remain distinguishable.

requirements.title: Cisco family pathways
requirements.behaviour: Connect the existing eight Cisco-oriented profiles to playable cloud, dedicated/premises, CC, CPaaS, device, provider, government and local-speech choices.
acceptance: Each of the eight families has at least one representative playable path tested through the campaign UI, with meaningful eligibility, cost, operating or compatibility behaviour linked to its source requirement.
Cloud, dedicated and on-premises resources are not interchangeable labels.
Remaining source obligations stay visible; shared implementation is not proof of every distinctive feature.

requirements.title: Channel and partner roles
requirements.behaviour: Supplier, carrier/SP, distributor, reseller, MSP, integrator, BPO and customer roles change authority, cost, workload or commercial access.
acceptance: Each role appears in at least one playable procurement or operating decision.
An MSP has shared staff/capital; an SP has numbering/interconnect capacity; a BPO supplies skills/schedules and people, not just licences.
A distributor/partner qualification changes a term or accessible offer; a logo alone is insufficient.

requirements.title: Third-party ecosystem
requirements.behaviour: Make compatibility, operating effort and specialist capabilities determine useful third-party purchases.
acceptance: Provisioning, assurance, room interop, SBC/carrier, recording/compliance, WFM/quality and AI/API categories each have at least one costed, outcome-changing path.
Preserve all 51 actor records and stable mappings; list each actor as implemented, shared with evidence, or pending.
Do not create a separate setup screen for every supplier or treat distinct behaviours as a name reskin.

requirements.title: CC people and quality
requirements.behaviour: Keep licences, people, skills, schedules, presence and digital concurrency independent. Preserve current costed coaching and quality receipts.
acceptance: A licensed queue without eligible people cannot handle the same workload as a staffed queue.
Coaching temporarily removes useful capacity, costs the authored amount once, and changes capability only after completion.
Quality review is evaluated from evidence in Campaign; authoring raw rubric scores remains Training/Lab.

requirements.title: Meetings, rooms and video
requirements.behaviour: Room/calendar/identity/device/interop/codec dependencies affect joining and supported quality.
acceptance: Native, interop and browser joining have declared feature subsets and capacity/cost consequences.

Implement scheduled, active and completed/failed meeting sessions with duration, occupancy, effective media and capture. The existing lastMeeting join check is an explicit probe and cannot satisfy actual video delivery.
A licence alone cannot create a physical room, staffed support or compatible media.
Local media resources change supported load or resilience without becoming an unrestricted substitute for a cloud service.

requirements.title: Information and transcription
requirements.behaviour: Capture, processing, quality/language, storage, access, retention and locality are separate obligations.
acceptance: A transcript requires eligible source capture, processor/model capacity and an allowed data path.
Cloud and local processing create a cost, delay, language/quality or dependency tradeoff.
Storage/backup/keys/admin/support boundaries remain independently inspectable; a transcript cannot be typed into success.

requirements.title: CPaaS and digital journeys
requirements.behaviour: Offer purchasable workflows with channel accounts, rate limits, per-use cost, retry behaviour and human handoff.
acceptance: One campaign job crosses an asynchronous channel/API workflow and resolves or fails from actual execution.
A retry cannot charge or resolve the customer twice outside explicit provider billing terms.
A human handoff retains customer context and uses genuine CC capacity.

requirements.title: On-premises and physical dependencies
requirements.behaviour: Retain real transport, local platforms, power, hardware and survivability when they change UC outcomes.
acceptance: Local/on-premises choices have setup, capacity, support and lifecycle costs.
A dependency outage changes only the workloads that depend on it; a supported local path can continue.
Keep the optional SP game separate; do not force carrier-network construction before the first SMB service.

requirements.title: Pure rendering and shared dispatch
requirements.behaviour: UI, worker, automation and MCP use the same validated rules; rendering is a read-only projection.
acceptance: Repeated render/inspect/select operations do not alter model revision, time, cash or randomness.
All campaign intents pass the shared validator and retain tenant authority and expectedRevision checks.
A new factory is included in browser, Node and worker assembly with matching behaviour.

requirements.title: Exactly-once time and persistence
requirements.behaviour: Save committed state and guard worker replies, time batches and cross-tab editing ownership.
acceptance: A stale worker result cannot replace a newer command or charge an interval twice.
Save/restore during a call, project, incident and pending bill reproduces the next outcome.
Losing the lock becomes visibly read-only/paused; storage failure preserves an exportable run.

requirements.title: Bounded long-play histories
requirements.behaviour: Replace the portfolio hard-stop at 2,000 journal entries with bounded history and durable summaries/checkpoints.
acceptance: A 2,001-minute multi-customer run does not hit the old journal limit and restores correctly.

A documented 20-active-customer, 10,000-minute headless fixture has nonzero sustained workload, recurring settlement and at least one change/incident. It preserves totals, obligations, monotonic IDs and deterministic continuation; inactive roots do not qualify.
Bound case, record, trace and receipt histories as well as the portfolio journal using valid archival summaries/checkpoints or tombstones; retain active obligations and required lineage.
UI sampling may be reduced under load; simulation outcomes and billing cannot be dropped.

requirements.title: Static build and usable deployment path
requirements.behaviour: Keep the browser-only static build and existing internationalisation/offline structure.
acceptance: The intended /series-of-calls/ path loads its own assets and language strings.
After successful cache installation, a supported offline reload preserves the available game.
No mandatory backend, login, external AI/API call or new framework is introduced for this rebuild.

requirements.title: Source and requirement accounting
requirements.behaviour: Preserve immutable source packs, MIT notices, history, stable mapping IDs and outstanding obligations.
acceptance: All 25 existing view mappings and six tutorial mappings receive an explicit new placement.
The 3,454-row catalogue remains intact; each implemented distinctive behaviour links to executed evidence.
No release/gate weakening or exclusion approval is bundled into the UI change.

requirements.title: Visible-UI commercial journeys
requirements.behaviour: Exercise real controls on the actual candidate build, not only DOM strings or direct dispatch.
acceptance: Record fresh start, alternative plan, incident, bill, renewal/exit and shared-resource expansion for the SMB opening.
Record one complete journey for enterprise, government and defence with distinct constraints.
Screenshots cover new game, cost comparison, active service, incident and post-billing expansion at desktop/mobile sizes.

requirements.title: Behavioural regression and gates
requirements.behaviour: Run the existing verification ladder on the changed behaviours and declared candidate.
acceptance: Include positive, meaningful failure and recovery cases for each new mechanic plus targeted lifecycle/economy repros.
Run required worker/save/communications, evidence, coverage, gate mutation, translation and build checks according to repository policy.
Report exact results and current blockers; never rename a failed full-release gate to a pass.

requirements.title: Human pilot and honest handoff
requirements.behaviour: Prepare an exploratory upstream/port comparison and report implementation evidence separately from human evidence.
acceptance: Provide a 6–8-person counterbalanced protocol measuring clarity, choice, consequence and changed-plan behaviour.
Do not claim people tested the game unless they actually did; human evidence stays pending until then.
Handoff distinguishes playable UI revision, remaining full-conversion obligations, browser verification and publication status.
